facts.statement: Notosuchus was a terrestrial animal that lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was terrestrial, living approximately 85 million years ago in the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Notosuchus was first named in 1896 and holds the distinction of being the first known notosuchian.
facts.quote: First named in 1896, Notosuchus was the first known notosuchian.

facts.statement: Fossilized remains of Notosuchus have been found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Its fossilised remains have been found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: A second species, N. lepidus, was named in 1957.
facts.quote: A second species, N. lepidus, was named in 1957.

facts.statement: The dentition of N. terrestris was heterodont, consisting of incisiform, caniniform, and molariform teeth.
facts.quote: The dentition of N. terrestris were heterodont and consisted of incisiform, caniniform, and molariform teeth.

facts.statement: The teeth of N. terrestris possessed exceptionally thick cementum compared to other crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: The teeth of N. terrestris had exceptionally thick cementum compared to other crocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: Notosuchus was relatively small in size.
Its skull was triangular in dorsal view, with a high snout that was quadrangular in cross-section and anterior external nares.
facts.quote: Su cráneo era triangular en vista dorsal, el hocico era alto, cuadrangular en sección transversal, con fosas nasales externas anteriores.

facts.statement: It was characterized by heterodont dentition with a wide range of morphologies in its posterior teeth.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por la presencia de una dentición heterodonta con una amplia gama de morfologías en sus dientes posteriores.

facts.statement: Some authors infer the presence of feeding mechanisms in Notosuchus that contrast with those of other crocodyliform groups, including modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Esta característica ha llevado a algunos autores a inferir la presencia de mecanismos de alimentación que contrastan con los de otros grupos de crocodiliformes (incluidos los crocodilianos actuales).

facts.statement: These terrestrial animals lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Coniacian or Santonian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Se trataba de animales terrestres que vivieron hace aproximadamente 85 millones de años, durante la época del Coniaciense o el Santoniense, en el Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: The time range for Notosuchus is the Santonian, spanning from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Bonaparte considered Notosuchia to be a suborder of Protosuchia based on basicranial characteristics in his 1991 study.
facts.quote: Bonaparte (1991), amplió la descripción de la anatomía craneana de Notosuchus, y a partir de características del basicráneo consideró a Notosuchia como un infraorden de Protosuchia.

facts.statement: Notosuchus shares three derived dental characters with Mariliasuchus amarali and Sphagesaurus huenei, suggesting these three taxa are more closely related to each other than to other crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Notosuchus comparten tres caracteres derivados con Mariliasuchus amarali y Sphagesaurus huenei del Cretácico Superior de Brasil, lo que respaldo las sugerencias que presentan a estos tres taxones como más estrechamente relacionados entre sí que con otros crocodiliformes.

facts.statement: The parent group of Notosuchus is Sphagesauria.
Analysis allowed researchers to infer a terrestrial lifestyle with an upright posture, propalinal jaw movement, and omnivorous or even herbivorous habits.
facts.quote: permitió inferir un modo de vida con adaptaciones al medio terrestre, con una postura erguida, con movimiento mandibular propalinal, y hábitos omnívoros o incluso herbívoros.
